definitions.explanation: Items that are no longer useful in their current form and have been discarded or set aside for disposal, recycling, or repurposing.

examples.japanese: {廃品|はいひん}⟦{回収|かいしゅう}→回収：03019_kaishuu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎月|まいつき}→毎月：00732_maitsuki⟧⟦{第|だい}{一|いち}→第一：19377_daiichi⟧⟦{土曜日|どようび}→土曜日：00621_doyoubi⟧です。
examples.english: Scrap collection is on the first Saturday of every month.

examples.japanese: {廃品|はいひん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{利用|りよう}して→利用する：21735_riyousuru⟧⟦アート→アート：10713_aato⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: To make art using discarded materials.

examples.japanese: ⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{廃品|はいひん}⟦{回収|かいしゅう}→回収：03019_kaishuu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{古新聞|ふるしんぶん}や⟦{段|だん}ボール→段ボール：18885_danbooru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}めた→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧。
examples.english: We collected old newspapers and cardboard in the school's scrap drive.

notes:
A compound of {廃|はい} (waste, discard) + ⟦{品|ひん}→品：03712_hin⟧ (goods, items). Most commonly appears in the phrase {廃品回収|はいひんかいしゅう} (scrap/waste collection).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {廃品|はいひん}⟦{回収|かいしゅう}→回収：03019_kaishuu⟧: scrap collection, waste collection drive
- {廃品|はいひん}⟦{回収|かいしゅう}→回収：03019_kaishuu⟧⟦{業者|ぎょうしゃ}→業者：13130_gyousha⟧: scrap collector, junk dealer
- {廃品|はいひん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}める→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧: to collect scrap/waste
- {廃品|はいひん}⟦{利用|りよう}→利用：01752_riyou⟧: reuse of waste materials

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, {廃品回収|はいひんかいしゅう} (scrap collection drives) are commonly organized by neighborhood associations, schools, or community groups as fundraising activities. Old newspapers, magazines, cardboard, and aluminum cans are typical items collected.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{廃棄物|はいきぶつ}→廃棄物：04634_haikibutsu⟧: waste, refuse — more formal/technical term for waste in general
- ⟦{粗大|そだい}ゴミ→粗大ゴミ：08045_sodaigomi⟧: oversized garbage — large items like furniture that require special disposal
- ⟦{不用品|ふようひん}→不用品：03146_fuyouhin⟧: unwanted items — things no longer needed but not necessarily waste
